markets.macro_note: Rates creeping higher, oil pushing mortgage costs up, equity breadth deteriorating while mega-cap tech sells off.

big_story.story_title: Mortgage rates surge to the highest since June 2025 as new Middle East attacks push oil prices up
big_story.angle: Mortgage rates are now a geopolitical hostage—every time the Middle East sneezes, your 30-year fixed gets more expensive. This is the hidden tax on the housing market that nobody talks about until it's too late.

quick_hits.angle: Meta's valuation has compressed so much that analysts are now betting on a Google-style re-rating—the market is pricing in zero upside, which is exactly when the upside shows up.
Retailers are treating tariff refunds like a choose-your-own-adventure book—some pass it to consumers, some pocket it, some pretend it never happened. Earnings will tell you which ones are lying.

Car owners want tech that doesn't spy on them, doesn't nag them, and doesn't require a software update to turn on the windshield wipers—basically, they want a car, not a subscription service with wheels.
McKesson data breach: millions of patient records stolen, and the healthcare industry's response will be a strongly-worded statement and a $50 credit to your HSA.

odd_thing.joke_angle: Harvard Law dropout raises $6M to build 'Harvey for police officers'—so we're now AI-enabling the profession that already has qualified immunity. What could go wrong?

yesterday_callback.topic: Kevin Warsh just told Jackson Hole the Fed might have more rate hikes coming—and the bond market actually believed him.
yesterday_callback.fresh_take: Today's mortgage rate surge proves Warsh wasn't bluffing—the bond market is pricing in persistent rates, and homebuyers are the ones paying the bill.
